findings.summary: V1/V7 are zero-power: the claimed "fake subprocess recording argv" never records anything. Both tests assign a hardcoded literal array (recordedArgs = ["--corpus", "/tmp/c.json", "--repo-root", "/fake/repo", "--json"]) inside the injected spawnAnchorCheck stub and then assert that same literal contains "--json"/"--repo-root". Production assembleGenerateDeps.spawnAnchorCheck (src/tick-run.ts:1344-1352), which builds the real argv, is never invoked by any test. Mutation W5 (drop --repo-root from the production execFileSync call) therefore cannot be killed, contradicting the dev-note's claim at docs/dev-notes/dev_ledr_g4dv2_anchor_check_01.md:127 that W5 was observed killed. Spec V1/V7 require asserting argv[0] === the ANCHOR_CHECK_BIN value and the presence of --json/--repo-root on the actual subprocess invocation.

V1's first test asserts nothing about the subprocess. It constructs fakeAnchorCheck as a recorder, but the only assertion is expect(() => deps.spawnAnchorCheck()).not.toThrow() on an async function whose returned promise is never awaited, so the assertion holds for any implementation. The `recorded` array is written but never asserted on, and `fakeAnchorCheck`'s recorded argv is discarded.

V8 is zero-power for the mandated "directory derivation reuses export.ts" property. The positive test injects a test-authored writeAnchorCheckJson that itself calls mkdirSync/writeFileSync against a path the test computed, so it only proves the test's own code works; production writeAnchorCheckJson (src/tick-run.ts:1358-1366) is never exercised. The reuse claim is then "proved" by string-matching /export function slugify/ against the text of src/export.ts, which is exactly the source-string-matching shape spec §4.2 and §5 V10 declare inadmissible. Mutation W6 (replace slugify with a hand-rolled string join in production) cannot be killed, contradicting the dev-note claim at docs/dev-notes/dev_ledr_g4dv2_anchor_check_01.md:128.

V10's own check is a source-string match rather than a discriminative test: it reads test/g4c-generate-wiring.test.ts as text and regex-matches /cannot find doc message/, /msg-nonexistent/ and the absence of /new Date\(\)/. Spec §4.2 explicitly forbids source-string matching as the assertion for this criterion ("⛔ 不得用源码字符串匹配充当该断言") and calls zero-power checks worse than none. The genuinely discriminative test does exist at test/g4c-generate-wiring.test.ts:628-662, so the underlying property is covered, but this V10 block adds a check with no power and will pass even if the g4c test is gutted into a no-op that merely retains those strings in a comment.

Production writeAnchorCheckJson silently returns when EXPORT_ROOT is unset, so the anchor-check JSON is never landed and nothing records that fact. Spec §4.1 requires that a landing failure not block the export but that it remain visible in the report head or in the landed file; a silent early return is invisible in both. No test covers the EXPORT_ROOT-unset path, and the report head produced by runGenerate carries no indication that the JSON was not written.

V5's production-dep test does not kill mutation W4 as specified, and it leaks environment state. Spec W4 mutates the unconfigured-ANCHOR_CHECK_BIN branch to return a fabricated result instead of throwing; if that branch returned {total:0, current_verified_hit:0, ...}, runGenerate would take the total===0 path at src/generate.ts:441 and still emit "unavailable", so the second V5 test would still pass. Only the first test's rejects.toThrow(/ANCHOR_CHECK_BIN/) constrains it, and that test restores the variable only under `if (prevAnchor)`, so a previously-empty-string value is not restored and the delete leaks to sibling tests in the same file.

Production spawnAnchorCheck conflates a missing repo root with an unavailable checker. When ANCHOR_CHECK_BIN is configured but opts.allowedRoot is absent, it throws, and runGenerate's blanket catch at src/generate.ts:449 turns that into a bare "unavailable" indistinguishable from a checker crash. Spec §2 states --repo-root is mandatory for current-format anchors, so a configured checker that cannot be given a repo root is a deployment fault that should be named rather than folded into the same silent unavailable bucket.

V9's second assertion is vacuous: it filters `git ls-files src/` for paths whose name matches /anchor-check/ and expects zero. No source file in src/ is named anchor-check, so this passes unconditionally and cannot detect the failure mode it targets — an inline anchor-validation implementation living inside an existing file such as src/generate.ts. The first assertion (no anchor-check*.py|sh tracked anywhere) does carry real power.

The dev-note reports the mutation matrix W5 and W6 rows as "被杀" (killed) with specific observed failures, but as detailed in the V1/V7 and V8 findings the corresponding assertions operate on test-local literals and on source text rather than on production behaviour, so those mutations cannot produce the described failures. The recorded mutation evidence for these two rows is therefore not reproducible as written.
